title.zh: 卷一百六十九 列傳第五十六: 賀仁傑 賈昔剌 劉哈剌八都魯 石抹明里 謝仲溫 高觿 張九思 王伯勝
title.en: Volume 169 Biographies 56: He Renjie, Jia Xila, Liu Halabadoulu, Shi Momingli, Xie Zhongwen, Gao Xi, Zhang Jiusi, Wang Bosheng
title.raw: 卷一百六十九 列傳第五十六: 賀仁傑 賈昔剌 劉哈剌八都魯 石抹明里 謝仲溫 高觿 張九思 王伯勝 Volume 169 Biographies 56: He Renjie, Jia Xila, Liu Halabadoulu, Shi Momingli, Xie Zhongwen, Gao Xi, Zhang Jiusi, Wang Bosheng

sentences.zh: 賀仁傑

translations.literal: He Renjie
translations.idiomatic: He Renjie

sentences.zh: 賀仁傑，字寬甫，其先河東隰州人，祖種德徒關中，遂為京兆鄠人。

translations.literal: He Renjie, styled Kuanfu. His ancestors were people of Xi Prefecture in Hedong; his grandfather Zhongde moved to Guanzhong and thus became a resident of Hu in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He Renjie, whose style name was Kuanfu, came from a family originally of Xi Prefecture in Hedong. His grandfather Zhongde relocated to Guanzhong, and the family thereafter were natives of Hu in the Jingzhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 父賁，有材略，善攻戰，數從軍有功。

translations.literal: His father Fen had talent and strategy, was skilled at assault warfare, and repeatedly followed campaigns with merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fen was gifted and resourceful, excelled in offensive warfare, and won repeated distinction on campaign.

sentences.zh: 關中兵後積尸滿野，賁買地金天門外，為大塚收瘞之。

translations.literal: After warfare in Guanzhong, corpses piled the fields; Fen bought land outside the Golden Heaven Gate and built a great mound to gather and inter them.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of war in Guanzhong, the dead lay heaped across the countryside. Fen purchased ground outside the Golden Heaven Gate and raised a great burial mound to collect and lay them to rest.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞者，爭輦屍來葬，復以私錢勞之。

translations.literal: Those who heard from near and far vied to cart corpses for burial; he again used private funds to reward them.
translations.idiomatic: People far and near, hearing of it, hurried to bring bodies by cart for burial, and he again paid them out of his own purse as a reward.

sentences.zh: 嘗治室於毀垣中，得白金七千五百兩，謂其妻鄭曰：「語云：匹夫無故獲千金，必有非常之禍。」

translations.literal: Once, while repairing a room amid ruined walls, he obtained seven thousand five hundred taels of silver and said to his wife Zheng: "The saying goes: when a common man without cause receives a thousand in gold, there must be an extraordinary calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while building a room among ruined walls, he unearthed seven thousand five hundred taels of silver. He told his wife Zheng, "As the proverb says, when an ordinary man comes by a fortune for no reason, some extraordinary misfortune is sure to follow."

sentences.zh: 時世祖以皇太弟受詔徵雲南，駐軍六盤山，乃持五千兩往獻之，世祖曰：「天以賜汝，焉用獻！」

translations.literal: At that time the Founder, as Imperial Younger Brother, had received orders to campaign in Yunnan and was encamped at Liupan Mountain; he then took five thousand taels to present them. The Founder said: "Heaven gave this to you—why present it!"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Kublai, still serving as imperial younger brother, had been ordered to campaign in Yunnan and was encamped on Liupan Mountain. Fen took five thousand taels to present to him. Kublai said, "Heaven bestowed this on you—why bring it to me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「殿下新封秦，金出秦地，此天以授殿下，臣不敢私，願以助軍。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Highness was newly enfeoffed as Prince of Qin; the gold came from Qin territory—this is Heaven bestowing it on Your Highness. Your servant dares not keep it privately and wishes to assist the army."
translations.idiomatic: Fen answered, "Your Highness has only lately been enfeoffed as Prince of Qin, and this silver came from Qin soil—it is Heaven's gift to you. I dare not keep it for myself and wish to devote it to the army."

sentences.zh: 且言其子仁傑可用狀，即召入宿衛。

translations.literal: He also reported that his son Renjie was capable in certain ways, and Renjie was immediately summoned into the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also described his son Renjie's qualifications for service, and Renjie was at once summoned into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 其軍帥怒賁不先白己而專獻金，下賁獄。

translations.literal: The army commander was angry that Fen had not informed him first but presented the gold on his own, and had Fen imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The army commander was furious that Fen had presented the silver without first reporting to him and had Fen thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之，大怒，執帥將殺之，以勳舊而止。

translations.literal: The Founder heard of this, became greatly angry, seized the commander and was about to execute him, but stopped because the man was an old meritorious follower.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai heard of it he was enraged, seized the commander, and was about to put him to death, but stayed his hand because the man was a veteran of long service.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，賜賁金符，總管京兆諸軍奧魯，卒，贈輸忠立義功臣、銀青榮祿大夫、大司徒，追封雍國公，諡貞獻。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, he granted Fen a gold tally and made him overseer of all military households of Jingzhao; on his death he was posthumously given the title Meritous Minister who Conveys Loyalty and Establishes Righteousness, Silver-Green Grandee of Glorious Emolument, and Grand Minister of Education, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yong with posthumous name Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: After Kublai ascended the throne he granted Fen a gold tally and appointed him to oversee all military households in Jingzhao. When Fen died he was posthumously honored as a meritous minister who conveyed loyalty and upheld righteousness, given the rank of Silver-Green Grandee of Glorious Emolument and Grand Minister of Education, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Yong, and given the temple name Zhenxian.

sentences.zh: 仁傑從世祖，南征雲南，北征乃顏，皆著勞績。

translations.literal: Renjie followed the Founder, campaigning south against Yunnan and north against Nayan, and in both distinguished himself with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie followed Kublai on the southern campaign into Yunnan and the northern campaign against Nayan, earning distinction in both.

sentences.zh: 後與董文忠居中事上，同志協力，知無不言，言無不聽，多所裨益，而言不外洩，帝深愛重之。

translations.literal: Later he and Dong Wenzhong attended on the emperor at court, of one mind and cooperating; what they knew they did not fail to speak, and what they spoke was not left unheard—much was benefited, and their words did not leak outside; the emperor deeply loved and valued them.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Dong Wenzhong served the emperor at court in close concert. Nothing they knew went unsaid, and nothing they said went unheeded; their counsel proved of great benefit, and it never leaked beyond the palace. The emperor cherished them deeply.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，宋平，惟川蜀久不下。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, Song was pacified, but Sichuan alone long would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Zhiyuan era the Song fell, yet Sichuan alone held out for years.

sentences.zh: 四川制置使張珏守重慶，合州安撫使王立守釣魚山，相拒二十餘年。

translations.literal: Sichuan Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jue held Chongqing, and Hezhou Pacification Commissioner Wang Li held Diaoyu Mountain; they resisted each other for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue, pacification commissioner of Sichuan, held Chongqing, while Wang Li, pacification commissioner of Hezhou, held Diaoyu Mountain, and the two fronts defied the Yuan for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 詔建東西行樞密院，督兵進伐，合丹、闊里吉思領東院，攻釣魚山；

translations.literal: An edict ordered the establishment of Eastern and Western Branch Offices of the Privy Council to supervise troops in the advance; Kedan and Kulijisi led the Eastern Office to attack Diaoyu Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: An edict established Eastern and Western branch privy councils to direct the advance. Kedan and Kulijisi commanded the eastern council against Diaoyu Mountain;

sentences.zh: 不花、李德輝領西院，攻重慶。

translations.literal: Buhua and Li Dehui led the Western Office to attack Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Buhua and Li Dehui led the western council against Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 德輝分守成都，獲王立鈔卒張郃，縱之使諭立降。

translations.literal: Dehui garrisoned Chengdu separately, captured Wang Li's paper-money soldier Zhang He, and released him to instruct Li to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dehui held Chengdu with a detached force, captured Zhang He, a soldier on paper-money duty under Wang Li, and sent him back to urge Li to surrender.

sentences.zh: 立復遣張郃等奉蠟書告德輝，能自來即降。

translations.literal: Li again sent Zhang He and others bearing a sealed letter to tell Dehui that if he would come in person Li would surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Li sent Zhang He back with a sealed letter promising that if Dehui came in person he would submit.

sentences.zh: 德輝遂從五百騎至釣魚山，與東院同受立降。

translations.literal: Dehui then went with five hundred horsemen to Diaoyu Mountain and together with the Eastern Office received Li's surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dehui rode to Diaoyu Mountain with five hundred horsemen and, together with the eastern council, accepted Li's surrender.

sentences.zh: 東院復奏誅立，並言德輝越境邀功，下立長安獄。

translations.literal: The Eastern Office again memorialized to execute Li and also said Dehui had crossed his border to claim merit; Li was put in prison in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern council then memorialized for Li's execution and accused Dehui of crossing into their jurisdiction to steal credit. Li was thrown into prison in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 西院從事呂掞至都，以兵事告許衡，許衡告仁傑，仁傑為言於帝。

translations.literal: Western Office staff member Lü Yan arrived at the capital and reported the military affair to Xu Heng; Xu Heng told Renjie, and Renjie spoke on it to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yan, an aide on the western staff, reached the capital and laid the matter before Xu Heng; Xu Heng informed Renjie, and Renjie pleaded the case before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝召樞密臣責之曰：「汝等以人命為戲耶！

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the privy council ministers and reproached them: "Do you take human lives as a jest!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the privy council ministers and rebuked them: "Do you treat men's lives as a game?

sentences.zh: 今召王立，立生則已，死則汝等亦從之。」

translations.literal: Now I summon Wang Li—if Li lives, well and good; if he dies, you too shall follow him."
translations.idiomatic: I am summoning Wang Li now. If he lives, so be it; if he dies, you shall die with him."

sentences.zh: 立至，賜金虎符，仍以為合州安撫使。

translations.literal: When Li arrived, he was granted a gold tiger tally and again appointed Pacification Commissioner of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li arrived the emperor granted him a gold tiger tally and restored him as pacification commissioner of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 帝一日召仁傑至榻前，出白金，謂之曰：「此汝父六盤所獻者，聞汝母來，可持以歸養。」

translations.literal: One day the emperor summoned Renjie before the couch, produced silver, and said to him: "This is what your father presented at Liupan; hearing your mother is coming, you may take it home to support her."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor called Renjie to his couch, produced the silver, and said, "This is what your father presented at Liupan. I hear your mother is on her way—you may take it home to provide for her."

sentences.zh: 辭不許，乃歸白母，盡散之宗族。

translations.literal: He declined but was not permitted; he then returned and told his mother and distributed it all among the clan.
translations.idiomatic: He declined, but the emperor would not hear of it. Renjie went home, told his mother, and distributed the whole sum among his kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 帝欲選民間童女充后宮；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to select young girls from among the people to fill the inner palace;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor proposed selecting young girls from the populace for the inner palace,

sentences.zh: 及有司買物，多非其土產；

translations.literal: and when government offices purchased goods, much was not local produce;
translations.idiomatic: and when government offices made purchases that were often not local products;

sentences.zh: 山后鹽禁，久為民害，皆奏罷之。

translations.literal: and the salt monopoly in the region north of the mountains had long been a harm to the people—he memorialized to abolish all of these.
translations.idiomatic: and the salt monopoly north of the Yan Mountains had long oppressed the people—Renjie memorialized to abolish each of these measures.

sentences.zh: 民為之立祠。

translations.literal: The people erected shrines to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people raised shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 十七年，上都留守闕，宰相擬廷臣以十數，皆不納，帝顧仁傑曰：「無以易卿者。」

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the post of Shangdu garrison commander was vacant; the chief ministers proposed a dozen court officials, but none was accepted; the emperor turned to Renjie and said: "There is no one to replace you."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the post of Shangdu garrison commander fell vacant. The chief ministers nominated a dozen court officials, but the emperor rejected them all and said to Renjie, "No one can take your place."

sentences.zh: 特授正議大夫、上都留守，兼本路總管、開平府尹。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Grand Master of Correct Counsel, Shangdu garrison commander, concurrently circuit intendant and prefect of Kaiping.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie was specially appointed Grand Master of Correct Counsel and Shangdu garrison commander, with concurrent duties as circuit intendant and prefect of Kaiping.

sentences.zh: 明年，賜三珠虎符，進資德大夫，兼虎賁親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted a three-pearl tiger tally, promoted to Grand Master of Assisting Virtue, and made concurrent commander of the Tiger Guard personal army.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received a three-pearl tiger tally, was promoted to Grand Master of Assisting Virtue, and was made concurrent commander of the Tiger Guard personal army.

sentences.zh: 尋加榮祿大夫、中書右丞，留守如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was further given Grand Master of Glorious Emolument and made right vice chancellor of the Secretariat, his garrison command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was further promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Emolument and appointed right vice chancellor of the Secretariat while retaining his garrison post.

sentences.zh: 尚書省立，桑哥用事，奏上都留守司錢穀多失實。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, Sangge held power and memorialized that the Shangdu garrison office's revenue and grain accounts were largely false.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue was established and Sangge came to power, he reported that the Shangdu garrison office's fiscal accounts were largely fraudulent.

sentences.zh: 召留守忽剌忽耳及仁傑廷辨，仁傑曰：「臣漢人，不能禁吏戢姦，致錢穀多耗傷，臣之罪。」

translations.literal: The garrison commanders Hulahuer and Renjie were summoned for court debate; Renjie said: "Your servant is a Han Chinese and could not restrain clerks and curb wrongdoing, causing much waste in revenue and grain—this is my crime."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the garrison commanders Hulahuer and Renjie to argue the case at court. Renjie said, "I am a Han Chinese and failed to restrain my clerks and curb corruption, which led to heavy losses in revenue and grain—that is my fault."

sentences.zh: 忽剌忽耳曰：「臣為長，印在臣手，事未有不關白而能行者，臣之罪。」

translations.literal: Hulahuer said: "Your servant is the chief; the seal is in my hand—nothing could be done without reporting to me—this is my crime."
translations.idiomatic: Hulahuer said, "I am the senior officer and hold the seal in my hand. Nothing could have been done without my approval—that is my fault."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「以爵讓人者有之，未有爭引咎歸己者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "There are those who yield rank to others, but never any who vie to take blame upon themselves."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Men have been known to yield rank to others, but never to compete in shouldering blame."

sentences.zh: 置勿問。

translations.literal: He set the matter aside and did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the matter and pursued it no further.

sentences.zh: 仁傑在官五十餘年，為留守者居半，車駕春秋行幸，出入供億，未嘗致上怒。

translations.literal: Renjie served in office more than fifty years, half of it as garrison commander; when the imperial carriage traveled on spring and autumn progresses, the provisioning of comings and goings never once provoked the emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie held office for more than fifty years, half of that time as Shangdu garrison commander. Through the emperor's spring and autumn progresses he managed provisioning for every arrival and departure without once drawing imperial displeasure.

sentences.zh: 其妻劉沒，帝欲為娶貴族，固辭，乃娶民間女，已而喪明，夫妻相敬如初，未嘗置媵妾。

translations.literal: His wife Liu died; the emperor wished to marry him to a noble family, but he firmly declined and took a commoner's daughter instead; later he lost his sight, yet husband and wife respected each other as at first and he never took a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife Liu died the emperor wished to marry him into a noble house, but he firmly declined and took a woman of common birth instead. Later he went blind, yet he and his wife remained as devoted to each other as before, and he never kept a concubine.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，年七十二，請老，拜光祿大夫、平章政事，商議陝西行中書省事，賜白金、楮幣、錦袍、玉帶，歸第。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade, at age seventy-two, he requested retirement and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Blessings and Grand Councillor to deliberate on affairs of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat; he was granted silver, paper currency, brocade robes, and a jade belt, and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Dade era, at seventy-two, he asked to retire and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Blessings and grand councillor to deliberate on affairs of the Shaanxi branch secretariat. He was given silver, paper currency, brocade robes, and a jade belt, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 以子勝襲上都留守、虎賁指揮使。

translations.literal: His son Sheng inherited the posts of Shangdu garrison commander and Tiger Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng inherited his posts as Shangdu garrison commander and commander of the Tiger Guard.

sentences.zh: 後成宗崩，仁宗入清內難，念世祖舊臣，欲有所諮訪，召赴闕，行至樊橋而卒。

translations.literal: Later, when Chengzong died and Renzong entered to settle the inner turmoil, remembering the Founder's old ministers he wished to consult someone and summoned him to court; he died at Fan Bridge on the way.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Chengzong died and Renzong came to settle the succession crisis, he thought of Kublai's old ministers and wished to consult one of them. Renjie was summoned to court but died at Fan Bridge on the journey.

sentences.zh: 贈恭勤竭力功臣、儀同三司、太保、上柱國，追封雍國公，諡忠貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Meritous Minister of Respectful Diligence and Exhausted Effort, ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Grand Guardian, and Upper Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yong with posthumous name Zhongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as a meritous minister of respectful diligence and tireless effort, given ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, the rank of Grand Guardian and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Yong, and granted the temple name Zhongzhen.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，加贈推誠宣力翊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封奉元王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou he was further posthumously given the title Meritous Minister who Pushes Sincerity, Proclaims Power, and Assists the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, ceremonial opening of offices equal to the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yanyou era he received further posthumous honors as a meritous minister who pushed sincerity, proclaimed power, and assisted the mandate, together with the ranks of Grand Preceptor, ceremonial opening of offices equal to the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State, and was enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 子勝，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Sheng has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: ○賈昔剌

translations.literal: Jia Xila
translations.idiomatic: Jia Xila

sentences.zh: 子丑妮子，方幼時，世祖愛之，嘗坐之禦席傍。

translations.literal: His son Chou Niz, while still young, was loved by the Founder, who would seat him beside the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chou Niz was still a boy when Kublai took a liking to him and would have him sit beside the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 從征雲南，躍馬入水，斫戰船，破其軍，帝奇其勇敢，而戒其輕銳。

translations.literal: On the campaign in Yunnan he leaped his horse into the water, hacked at war boats, and broke the enemy army; the emperor marveled at his bravery but admonished his rash daring.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yunnan campaign he spurred his horse into the water, hacked at the enemy war boats, and routed their force. The emperor admired his courage but warned him against reckless daring.

sentences.zh: 己未，從伐宋，還自鄂州，卒。

translations.literal: In the year jiwei he followed the attack on Song, returned from Ezhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year he joined the campaign against the Song, returned from Ezhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 追封臨汾郡公，諡顯毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Linfen Commandery with posthumous name Xianyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Linfen commandery with the temple name Xianyi.

sentences.zh: 子虎林赤，智勇絕人。

translations.literal: His son Hulinchi was unmatched in wisdom and courage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hulinchi was a man of extraordinary wit and valor.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥之叛，出其家名馬以助官軍。

translations.literal: When Ariq Böke rebelled, he brought out his family's famous horses to assist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ariq Böke rebelled he contributed his family's finest horses to the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 從幸和林，中道值大風，晝晦，敵猝至，擊走之。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor to Karakorum, midway they met a great wind and daylight darkened; the enemy came suddenly and he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: While accompanying the emperor to Karakorum they were struck midway by a violent wind that darkened the day. The enemy appeared without warning, and he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 還，佩其大父金符，提點尚食、尚藥二局，歷尚膳使，兼司農。

translations.literal: On return he wore his grandfather's gold tally, supervised the Imperial Food and Imperial Medicine bureaus, served as Imperial Provisioner, and concurrently held the Ministry of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he wore his grandfather's gold tally, supervised the imperial food and medicine bureaus, served as imperial provisioner, and concurrently held office in the Ministry of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 嘗入侍，帝問治天下何為本，曰：「重農為本。」

translations.literal: Once while attending in service the emperor asked what should be the foundation of governing all under Heaven; he said: "Taking agriculture seriously is the foundation."
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending the emperor in service, he was asked what should be the foundation of governing the realm. He answered, "Agriculture must be the foundation."

sentences.zh: 何為先，曰：「用賢為先。

translations.literal: What should come first? he said: "Employing the worthy comes first.
translations.idiomatic: What should come first?" "Employing worthy men comes first.

sentences.zh: 用賢則天下治，重農則百姓足。」

translations.literal: Employ the worthy and all under Heaven is governed; take agriculture seriously and the hundred surnames are provided for."
translations.idiomatic: Employ the worthy and the realm is well governed; take agriculture seriously and the people are provided for."

sentences.zh: 帝深善之，超拜宣徽使，辭，改僉院事，仍領尚膳使，卒。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved this, promoted him in exception to the usual order to Commissioner of the Imperial Household, he declined, was changed to vice director of the court, still headed the Imperial Provisioner, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply pleased and promoted him out of turn to commissioner of the imperial household. He declined and was made vice director of the court instead, while continuing to head the imperial provisioner's office, and later died.

sentences.zh: 子禿堅不花，襲世職為尚藥、尚食局提點，世祖以故家子，獨奇之，謂他日可大用，使在左右。

translations.literal: His son Tujianbuhua inherited the hereditary post as supervisor of the Imperial Medicine and Imperial Food bureaus; the Founder, as a son of an old family, singled him out for wonder, saying he could be greatly used another day, and kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tujianbuhua inherited the hereditary post supervising the imperial medicine and food bureaus. Kublai, seeing him as the scion of an old family, took a special interest in him, said he would be of great use one day, and kept him at his side.

sentences.zh: 從征乃顏，軍次杭海，敵猝至，帝令急擊之。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Nayan the army halted at Hang Hai; the enemy came suddenly and the emperor ordered a swift attack.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Nayan the army halted at Hang Hai when the enemy appeared without warning. The emperor ordered an immediate attack.

sentences.zh: 諸近侍見其勢盛，多畏避，禿堅不花即馳入其陣，疾戰，破走之，擒其首將以歸。

translations.literal: The close attendants, seeing the enemy's strength, mostly shrank back in fear; Tujianbuhua at once galloped into their formation, fought fiercely, routed them, and captured their chief general to return.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the close attendants, seeing how strong the enemy was, hung back in fear. Tujianbuhua galloped straight into their ranks, fought furiously, routed them, and brought back their chief commander as a captive.

sentences.zh: 移軍哈罕，大風，晝晦，敵兵千人，鼓譟以進，禿堅不花奮擊，身被十餘瘡，猶力戰，復大破之，帝奇其勇。

translations.literal: The army moved to Hahan; a great wind arose and daylight darkened; a thousand enemy soldiers advanced with drums and clamor; Tujianbuhua fought fiercely, received more than ten wounds, yet still battled hard, again routing them greatly; the emperor marveled at his courage.
translations.idiomatic: When the army moved to Hahan a great wind arose and day turned dark. A thousand enemy soldiers advanced with drums and shouting. Tujianbuhua fought on despite more than ten wounds, broke them again, and the emperor marveled at his valor.

sentences.zh: 杭海叛者請降，眾議以為親犯王師，宜誅之，禿堅不花獨曰：「杭海本吾人，或誘之以叛，豈其本心哉！

translations.literal: The Hang Hai rebels asked to surrender; the assembly debated that since they had personally offended the imperial army they should be executed; Tujianbuhua alone said: "Hang Hai were originally our people—perhaps someone lured them into rebellion; how could that be their true intent!
translations.idiomatic: When the Hang Hai rebels asked to surrender the council argued that, having directly attacked the imperial army, they deserved execution. Tujianbuhua alone said, "Hang Hai were originally our own people. Someone may have lured them into rebellion—that could hardly have been their true intent!

sentences.zh: 且兵法殺降不祥，宜赦之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, by military law killing those who surrender is inauspicious—they should be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, military law holds that killing those who surrender brings ill fortune. They should be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「禿堅不花議是。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Tujianbuhua's counsel is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Tujianbuhua is right."

sentences.zh: 以此益知其可用，升同僉宣徽院事。

translations.literal: From this he came to know even better that he could be used, and promoted him to associate vice director of the Imperial Household Court.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor knew even better that he could be relied upon and promoted him to associate vice director of the imperial household court.

sentences.zh: 每論政帝前，言直而氣不懾，帝亦知其直。

translations.literal: Whenever he discussed policy before the emperor his words were direct and his spirit unafraid; the emperor also knew he was direct.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he discussed policy before the emperor he spoke plainly and without fear, and the emperor knew him for a forthright man.

sentences.zh: 令察宿衛之士，有才器者以名聞，所論薦數十人，用之皆稱職，時論歸之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to examine the palace guard for men of talent and report their names; those he recommended numbered several tens, and all whom were employed proved competent—contemporary opinion accorded with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to survey the palace guard for men of talent and recommend them by name. He nominated several dozen, and every man appointed proved competent. Public opinion credited him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，諸侯王會於上京，凡芻餼宴享之節、賜予多寡、疏戚之分，無一不當其意，帝喜曰：「宣徽得禿堅不花足矣。」

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne the princes assembled at Shangdu; for all the protocols of fodder, provisions, banquets, and feasts, the amounts of gifts, and distinctions of near and distant kinship, not one failed to suit his intent; the emperor rejoiced and said: "For the Imperial Household, having Tujianbuhua is enough."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne the princes assembled at Shangdu. For every detail of fodder, provisions, banquets, gifts, and distinctions of kinship near and far, Tujianbuhua judged exactly to the emperor's liking. Chengzong said with satisfaction, "For the imperial household, Tujianbuhua alone is enough."

sentences.zh: 進同知宣徽院事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to associate director of the Imperial Household Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to associate director of the imperial household court.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝弗豫，召入侍疾，一食一飲，必嘗乃進。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor was unwell and summoned him to attend the illness; every food and drink he must taste before presenting.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when the emperor fell ill, he was summoned to attend him at the bedside. He tasted every meal and drink before it was served.

sentences.zh: 帝體既安，賜錢，不受，解衣賜之。

translations.literal: When the emperor's body had recovered he granted money, which was not accepted; he removed a garment and granted that instead.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had recovered he offered money, but Tujianbuhua would not take it, so the emperor gave him a robe from his own person instead.

sentences.zh: 嘗從巡幸，禁中衛士感奮有所欲言，帝命進而問之，皆曰：「臣等宿衛有年矣，日膳充、歲賜以時者，誠荷陛下厚恩，亦由宣徽有能官禿堅不花其人也。」

translations.literal: Once while accompanying a progress, palace guards stirred with emotion and wished to speak; the emperor ordered them forward to ask, and all said: "We have guarded for years; daily provisions full and yearly gifts on time—we truly bear Your Majesty's deep grace, but also because the Imperial Household has the capable officer Tujianbuhua."
translations.idiomatic: Once, on a progress, the palace guards were moved to speak up. The emperor had them come forward and asked what they wished to say. They all replied, "We have served in the guard for years. Our daily rations are ample and our annual gifts arrive on time. We owe Your Majesty's deep kindness, but we owe it as well to the capable officer Tujianbuhua of the imperial household."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜珠袍，超拜宣徽使。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, granted a pearl robe, and promoted him in exception to the usual order to Commissioner of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, granted him a pearl-embroidered robe, and promoted him out of turn to commissioner of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「先臣服勤，於茲三世矣，位不過僉佐，臣何敢有加於先臣乎！」

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "My forebears served diligently for three generations here, their posts not exceeding associate aides—how dare your servant rise above the former ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "My forebears served diligently for three generations, yet none rose above associate rank. How dare I surpass my ancestors!"

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其退讓，乃允其請。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his modest withdrawal and then granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his modesty and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 九年，北方乞祿倫部大雪，奏買駝馬，補其死損，出衣幣於內府，身往給之，全活者數万人，還，賜七寶笠。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the northern Qilulun tribes suffered heavy snow; he memorialized to purchase camels and horses to replace their dead losses, took robes and currency from the inner treasury, went in person to distribute them, and several tens of thousands were wholly preserved; on return he was granted a seven-jewel canopy hat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year heavy snow struck the Qilulun tribes of the north. He memorialized to purchase camels and horses to replace their losses, drew robes and currency from the inner treasury, went in person to distribute them, and saved several tens of thousands of lives. On his return he was granted a seven-jewel canopy hat.

sentences.zh: 十年，帝病甚，入侍疾愈謹。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the emperor's illness was severe; he attended the illness with ever greater care.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when the emperor's illness grew grave, he attended him with still greater care.

sentences.zh: 及大漸，內難將作，揆以正義，無所回撓。

translations.literal: When the end approached and inner turmoil was about to arise, he measured affairs by righteousness and bent to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: As the end approached and a succession crisis loomed, he held to righteousness and would not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne he was given the additional rank of Golden Purple Grandee of Splendid Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne he was given the additional rank of Golden Purple Grandee of Splendid Blessings.

sentences.zh: 廷祐四年，朔方又被風雪為災，禿堅不花請賑之如大德時，且出私家馬二百匹以為助，賜錢酬其價，不受，解御衣賜之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou the northern frontier again suffered wind and snow as disaster; Tujianbuhua requested relief as in the Dade era and also contributed two hundred private horses as aid; money was granted to compensate their price, which he did not accept; the emperor removed his imperial robe and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Yanyou era the northern frontier was again ravaged by wind and snow. Tujianbuhua asked for relief on the model of the Dade relief and contributed two hundred of his own horses as well. The emperor offered money to compensate their value, but he would not take it, so the emperor gave him a robe from his own person instead.

sentences.zh: 托恩幸以求賞者，輒抑弗予。

translations.literal: Those who relied on favor to seek rewards he always suppressed and did not grant.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought rewards by trading on imperial favor he consistently turned away.

sentences.zh: 帖失、王廷顯，皆同官也，帝賜帖失海舶，禿堅不花曰：「此軍國之所資，上不宜賜，下不宜受。」

translations.literal: Tieshi and Wang Tingxian were both colleagues; the emperor granted Tieshi a seagoing vessel; Tujianbuhua said: "This is what the army and state rely upon—the sovereign should not grant it, the subject should not receive it."
translations.idiomatic: Tieshi and Wang Tingxian were colleagues of his. When the emperor granted Tieshi a seagoing vessel, Tujianbuhua objected: "These are resources of the army and state. The throne should not give them away, and a subject should not accept them."

sentences.zh: 帝賜廷顯玉帶，廷顯欲取太官羊錢一萬五千緡充其價，又執不可。

translations.literal: The emperor granted Tingxian a jade belt; Tingxian wished to take fifteen thousand strings of sheep money from the Imperial Kitchen to cover its price, and he again held firm that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor granted Tingxian a jade belt, Tingxian wished to take fifteen thousand strings from the imperial kitchen's sheep fund to cover its value, and Tujianbuhua again refused to allow it.

sentences.zh: 於是怨之者眾。

translations.literal: From this those who resented him were many.
translations.idiomatic: From this he made many enemies.

sentences.zh: 七年，以疾去官。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，帖失竟譖殺之，後帖失以大逆伏誅，事乃白，贈推忠宣力守諒功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封冀國公，諡忠隱。

translations.literal: When Yingzong took the throne, Tieshi at last slandered him to death; later Tieshi was executed for great treason and the affair was cleared; he was posthumously given the title Meritous Minister who Pushes Loyalty, Proclaims Power, and Guards Good Faith, Grand Tutor, ceremonial opening of offices equal to the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with posthumous name Zhongyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong ascended the throne, Tieshi at last slandered him to his death. Later Tieshi was executed for high treason and the truth came out. Tujianbuhua was posthumously honored as a meritous minister who pushed loyalty, proclaimed power, and guarded good faith, given the ranks of Grand Tutor, ceremonial opening of offices equal to the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Ji, and granted the temple name Zhongyin.

sentences.zh: 後進封冀安王；

translations.literal: Later he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Ji'an;
translations.idiomatic: Later he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Ji'an;

sentences.zh: 加贈其曾祖昔剌推忠翊運功臣、金紫光祿大夫、太保，進封絳國公；

translations.literal: his great-grandfather Xila was further posthumously given the title Meritous Minister who Pushes Loyalty and Assists the Mandate, Golden Purple Grandee of Splendid Blessings, and Grand Guardian, advanced to Duke of Jiang;
translations.idiomatic: his great-grandfather Xila was further honored as a meritous minister who pushed loyalty and assisted the mandate, given the ranks of Golden Purple Grandee of Splendid Blessings and Grand Guardian, and advanced to Duke of Jiang;

sentences.zh: 祖醜妮子崇德效節功臣、儀同三司、太傅、柱國，追封絳國公；

translations.literal: his grandfather Chou Niz was given the title Meritous Minister of Honoring Virtue and Effecting Loyalty, ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies, Grand Tutor, and Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Jiang;
translations.idiomatic: his grandfather Chou Niz was honored as a meritous minister of honoring virtue and effecting loyalty, given ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, the ranks of Grand Tutor and Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Jiang;

sentences.zh: 父虎林赤推誠宣力守德功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，進封臨汾王。

translations.literal: his father Hulinchi was given the title Meritous Minister who Pushes Sincerity, Proclaims Power, and Guards Virtue, Grand Preceptor, ceremonial opening of offices equal to the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State, advanced to Prince of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: and his father Hulinchi was honored as a meritous minister who pushed sincerity, proclaimed power, and guarded virtue, given the ranks of Grand Preceptor, ceremonial opening of offices equal to the Three Excellencies, and Upper Pillar of the State, and advanced to Prince of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 子班卜、忽裡台、也速古、禿忽赤，皆至顯官。

translations.literal: His sons Banbu, Hulitai, Yesugu, and Tuhuchi all reached eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Banbu, Hulitai, Yesugu, and Tuhuchi all rose to eminent office.

sentences.zh: ○劉哈剌八都魯

translations.literal: Liu Halabadoulu
translations.idiomatic: Liu Halabadoulu

sentences.zh: 劉哈剌八都魯，河東人，本姓劉氏，家世業醫。

translations.literal: Liu Halabadoulu was a man of Hedong, originally surnamed Liu, his family for generations practicing medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Halabadoulu was a native of Hedong, originally of the Liu clan, with a family that had practiced medicine for generations.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，世祖駐蹕白海，以近臣言，得召見。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan the Founder was encamped at Bai Hai; on a close attendant's word he was summoned for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Zhiyuan era Kublai was encamped at Bai Hai. On a close attendant's recommendation he was summoned for an audience.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂其目有火光，異之，遂留侍左右，初賜名哈剌斡脫赤。

translations.literal: The Founder said his eyes had a fire-glow, found him strange, and kept him to attend at his side; he was first granted the name Harawotuochi.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said his eyes shone with a fiery light, found him remarkable, and kept him in attendance at his side. He was first granted the name Harawotuochi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢太醫院管勾。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to registrar of the Imperial Medical Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to registrar of the Imperial Medical Academy.

sentences.zh: 昔里吉叛，宗王別裡鐵穆而奉命往征之，帝諭哈剌八都魯曰：「當行者多避事，汝善醫，復習騎射，能從行乎？」

translations.literal: Shiregi rebelled; the imperial prince Beritemur was ordered to campaign against him; the emperor instructed Halabadoulu: "Many who should go shirk their duty—you are skilled in medicine and also practiced in riding and archery; can you follow on the campaign?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shiregi rebelled, Prince Beritemur was ordered to campaign against him. The emperor said to Halabadoulu, "Most of those who ought to go are shirking their duty. You are a skilled physician and also trained in riding and archery—can you join the expedition?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「事君不辭難，臣不行將何為！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Serving one's lord without declining difficulty—if your servant does not go, what shall he do!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "To serve one's lord is to accept hardship. If I do not go, what am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 即請授甲，帝曰：「汝安用甲？」

translations.literal: He at once requested armor; the emperor said: "What need have you of armor?"
translations.idiomatic: He immediately asked for armor. The emperor said, "What do you need armor for?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣願備一戰士。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant wishes to stand ready as a fighting man."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I wish to stand ready as a fighting man."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「醫，汝事也，甲不可得。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Medicine is your duty—armor cannot be granted."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Medicine is your duty. Armor is out of the question."

sentences.zh: 惟賜以環刀、弓矢、裘馬等物。

translations.literal: Only a ring-handled saber, bow and arrows, fur robes, horses, and such things were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was given only a ring-handled saber, bow and arrows, fur robes, horses, and the like.

sentences.zh: 將行，聞母疾，請歸省，帝命給驛而歸。

translations.literal: About to depart, he heard his mother was ill and requested leave to visit her; the emperor ordered relay stations provided for his return.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he learned his mother was ill and asked to visit her. The emperor ordered relay horses provided for the journey home.

sentences.zh: 既見母，不敢以遠役告，母亦微知之，謂曰：「汝第行，我疾安矣。」

translations.literal: Once he saw his mother he dared not tell her of the distant service; his mother also knew in part and said: "You need only go—my illness is settled."
translations.idiomatic: When he saw his mother he dared not tell her he was bound for a distant campaign. She had guessed as much and said, "Go. My illness is nothing."

sentences.zh: 遂即辭去，忍淚不下，而鼻血暴出，數里弗止，馳至王所。

translations.literal: He then took leave at once, holding back tears that would not fall, while noseblood burst forth and for several li would not stop; he galloped to the prince's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He took his leave at once, holding back tears, while blood poured from his nose and did not stop for several li. He galloped to join the prince.

sentences.zh: 一日，獵於野，有狐竄草中，王射之，不中，哈剌八都魯一發中之，王大喜。

translations.literal: One day while hunting in the wild a fox darted into the grass; the prince shot at it and missed; Halabadoulu with one shot hit it, and the prince was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: One day while hunting in the open country a fox darted into the grass. The prince shot and missed, but Halabadoulu brought it down with a single arrow, to the prince's great delight.

sentences.zh: 王妃有疾，與藥即愈，王又喜，奏為其府長吏。

translations.literal: The prince's consort had an illness; he gave medicine and she was quickly cured; the prince was pleased again and memorialized to make him chief administrator of his princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince's consort fell ill he gave her medicine and she recovered at once. The prince was pleased again and had him appointed chief administrator of his household.

sentences.zh: 及將戰，從王請甲，王曰：「上不與汝，我何敢與！」

translations.literal: When battle was about to begin he followed the prince in requesting armor; the prince said: "The sovereign did not grant it to you—how dare I grant it!"
translations.idiomatic: As battle approached he again asked the prince for armor. The prince said, "The emperor would not give it to you—how dare I?"

sentences.zh: 因留之，使領輜重。

translations.literal: He therefore kept him back and had him oversee baggage trains.
translations.idiomatic: He kept him behind instead and put him in charge of the baggage train.

sentences.zh: 哈剌八都魯不肯，曰：「大丈夫當效命行陣，乃守營帳如婦人耶！」

translations.literal: Halabadoulu would not accept this and said: "A great man should offer his life in the battle line—am I to guard the camp like a woman!"
translations.idiomatic: Halabadoulu refused. "A man should give his life on the battlefield," he said. "Am I to guard the camp like a woman?"

sentences.zh: 見有甲者，飲以酒，高價取之，明日，被以往。

translations.literal: Seeing one who had armor, he gave him wine and bought it at a high price; the next day he donned it and went forth.
translations.idiomatic: He found a man with armor, plied him with wine, and bought it at a high price. The next day he put it on and rode out.

sentences.zh: 王望見其介而馳走，使人問之，免冑曰：「我也。」

translations.literal: The prince saw his armor from afar and galloped away; he sent someone to ask, and Halabadoulu removed his helmet and said: "It is I."
translations.idiomatic: The prince saw his armor from afar and galloped away in alarm. When a messenger was sent to inquire, Halabadoulu removed his helmet and said, "It is I."

sentences.zh: 因慨然曰：「一人興善，萬人可激，我為萬人激耳！」

translations.literal: He then said with feeling: "When one man does good, ten thousand can be stirred—I am stirring the ten thousand!"
translations.idiomatic: He said with feeling, "When one man does good, ten thousand may be stirred to follow. I am stirring the ten thousand!"

sentences.zh: 中道，三遇賊，賊射之，皆不中。

translations.literal: Midway he three times met bandits; the bandits shot at him and all missed.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way he met bandits three times. They shot at him and missed every time.

sentences.zh: 王喜甚，解衣衣之曰：「此所以識也。」

translations.literal: The prince was greatly pleased, removed his garment and clothed him in it, saying: "This is how you shall be known."
translations.idiomatic: The prince was overjoyed, took off his own robe and gave it to him, and said, "Let this be your mark of recognition."

sentences.zh: 師次金山，路隘，頓兵未能進，有使者云自脫忽王所來，曰：「我受太祖分地，守此不敢失。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jin Mountain; the road was narrow and the troops could not advance; a messenger came saying he was from Prince Tuhu and said: "I received allotted lands from the Great Ancestor and guard them here, not daring to lose them.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jin Mountain, where the road was narrow and the troops could not advance. A messenger arrived claiming to come from Prince Tuhu and said, "I hold lands allotted by the Great Ancestor and guard them here. I dare not abandon them.

sentences.zh: 凡上所使與昔里吉之過我者，吾並飲食供給之，無異心也。

translations.literal: All who come from the court or from Shiregi passing by me, I alike supply with food and drink—I have no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whether envoys from the court or from Shiregi pass through my territory, I feed and supply them all alike. I bear no other intent.

sentences.zh: 且願見天子，而道遠無援，今聞王來甚喜，得一見可乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover I wish to see the Son of Heaven, but the road is far and I have no support; now hearing Your Highness has come I am greatly pleased—might I have one meeting?"
translations.idiomatic: I also wish to see the Son of Heaven, but the road is long and I have no support. Now that I hear Your Highness has come I am greatly pleased. Might we meet once?"

sentences.zh: 王以為信，左右曰：「此詐也，脫忽所居要害，殆與昔里吉為耳目，願勿聽。」

translations.literal: The prince believed him; those at his side said: "This is deception—Tuhu dwells in a strategic place and is likely Shiregi's eyes and ears; we beg you not to listen."
translations.idiomatic: The prince believed him, but his attendants said, "This is a ruse. Tuhu holds a strategic position and is likely Shiregi's eyes and ears. Do not heed him."

sentences.zh: 乃羈其人，遣兵間道窺之，獲其遊騎三十人，訊之得其情，知脫忽方飲酣。

translations.literal: They therefore detained the man, sent troops by a hidden path to spy, captured thirty of his roaming horsemen, questioned them and learned the truth, and knew Tuhu was then deep in drink.
translations.idiomatic: They detained the messenger and sent troops by a hidden path to reconnoiter. They captured thirty of his roaming horsemen, learned the truth from them, and discovered that Tuhu was then deep in his cups.

sentences.zh: 遂出其不意，進擊，大敗之，因獲昔里吉所遣使，知其不為備，又乘勢進擊，大破擒之，王乃命哈剌八都魯獻俘行宮。

translations.literal: They then struck by surprise, advanced to attack, and routed him greatly; they thereby captured an envoy Shiregi had sent, learned he was unprepared, again pressed the attack with momentum, broke and captured him greatly; the prince then ordered Halabadoulu to present captives at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: They struck by surprise, routed him, and captured an envoy Shiregi had sent. Learning that the enemy was unprepared, they pressed the attack again and won a great victory. The prince then ordered Halabadoulu to present the captives at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 帝見其瘠甚，輟御膳羊胾以賜，既拜受，先割其美者懷之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw he was very thin and set aside imperial mutton from the meal to grant him; having bowed and received it, he first cut the best portions and hid them in his bosom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw how gaunt he was and set aside mutton from the imperial meal as a gift. After bowing and accepting it, he cut off the best portions and hid them in his robe.

sentences.zh: 帝問其故，對曰：「臣始與母訣，今歸，母倖存，請以君賜遺之。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he replied: "Your servant first took leave of his mother; now returning, if my mother still lives, I beg to send her what the sovereign granted."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked why, he said, "When I left I took farewell of my mother. If she is still alive when I return, I beg to bring her what Your Majesty has granted."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其志，命自今凡賜之食，必先賜其母。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent and ordered that from now on whenever food was granted to him, his mother must be granted first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his devotion and ordered that from then on whatever food was granted to him must first be granted to his mother.

sentences.zh: 以功授和林等處宣慰副使，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed associate pacification commissioner of Karakorum and other places, with very generous grants.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed associate pacification commissioner of Karakorum and other regions, with lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，升同知宣慰司事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to associate director of the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was promoted to associate director of the pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，又升宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was further promoted to pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was further promoted to pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，海都犯邊，尚書省以和林屯糧，當得知緩急輕重者掌其出納，奏用怯伯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Haidu violated the frontier; the Ministry of Revenue, regarding the grain stored at Karakorum, memorialized that one who knows what is urgent or light in disbursement should oversee receipts and payments, and proposed using Qiebo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Haidu raided the frontier. The Ministry of Revenue, noting the grain stored at Karakorum, memorialized that someone who could judge what was urgent or expendable should control disbursements and proposed Qiebo for the post.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「錢穀非怯伯所知，哈剌斡脫赤可使也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Revenue and grain are not what Qiebo understands—Harawotuochi can be used for this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Revenue and grain are not Qiebo's strength. Harawotuochi will do."

sentences.zh: 進階嘉議大夫，職如故，使怯伯與俱。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master of Advising Counsel, his duties as before, with Qiebo sent along with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Advising Counsel with his duties unchanged, and Qiebo was sent along with him.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，海都兵至，皇子北安王使報怯伯，率其民避去。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year Haidu's army arrived; the prince Northern Pacification King sent word to Qiebo to lead his people away in avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year Haidu's army arrived. Prince Northern Pacification sent word to Qiebo to lead his people away to safety.

sentences.zh: 怯伯與哈剌八都魯南行六日，止八兒不剌，距海都軍五六十里。

translations.literal: Qiebo and Halabadoulu traveled south six days and halted at Ba'erbula, fifty or sixty li from Haidu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Qiebo and Halabadoulu marched south for six days and halted at Ba'erbula, fifty or sixty li from Haidu's army.

sentences.zh: 怯伯大懼曰：「事忽矣，不如順之。」

translations.literal: Qiebo was greatly afraid and said: "Matters have suddenly changed—better to submit to him."
translations.idiomatic: Qiebo was terrified and said, "Events have taken a sudden turn. We had better submit to him."

sentences.zh: 哈剌八都魯語其弟欽祖、榮祖曰：「怯伯有二心矣。」

translations.literal: Halabadoulu said to his younger brothers Qinzu and Rongzu: "Qiebo has a divided heart now."
translations.idiomatic: Halabadoulu told his younger brothers Qinzu and Rongzu, "Qiebo is already wavering."

sentences.zh: 遂潛遁，與探馬赤千戶忽剌思遇，從騎百餘人，問之，急剌思曰：「吾在海都軍中，聞怯伯反，宣慰脫身歸報天子，我故追以來。」

translations.literal: He then slipped away in secret and met the scout Hulas, chiliarch of the Red Guards, with a following of more than a hundred horsemen; questioning him, Hulas said: "I was in Haidu's army and heard Qiebo had turned rebel; the pacification commissioner escaped to report to the Son of Heaven—I therefore pursued to come."
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away secretly and met Hulas, a chiliarch of the Red Guard scouts, with more than a hundred horsemen. Hulas said, "I was in Haidu's army and heard Qiebo had turned traitor. The pacification commissioner escaped to report to the Son of Heaven, and I came in pursuit."

sentences.zh: 哈剌八都魯察其誠，與之謀，結陣乘高立於西南，令之曰：「吾將往責怯伯，汝曹勿動，見吾執弓而起，即相應也。」

translations.literal: Halabadoulu perceived his sincerity and plotted with him, forming ranks on high ground standing to the southwest, and ordered: "I shall go to reproach Qiebo—you must not move; when you see me draw the bow and rise, respond at once."
translations.idiomatic: Halabadoulu judged him sincere and plotted with him. They formed ranks on high ground to the southwest. He ordered, "I am going to confront Qiebo. Do not move until you see me draw my bow and rise—then act at once."

sentences.zh: 既見怯伯，怯伯盛言海都之令以威之。

translations.literal: Once he saw Qiebo, Qiebo spoke at length of Haidu's orders to intimidate him.
translations.idiomatic: When he met Qiebo, Qiebo spoke at length of Haidu's orders to intimidate him.

sentences.zh: 哈剌八都魯詭辭自解，得間，疾趨。

translations.literal: Halabadoulu used deceptive words to extricate himself, found an opening, and ran swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Halabadoulu answered evasively, found an opening, and ran.

sentences.zh: 忽剌思整陣以出，怯伯遣騎來追，屢拒卻之。

translations.literal: Hulas formed ranks and came out; Qiebo sent horsemen in pursuit and they repeatedly drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Hulas formed ranks and came out. Qiebo sent horsemen in pursuit, but they were driven back again and again.

sentences.zh: 道遇送軍裝者，因護之至鹽海。

translations.literal: On the road they met men delivering military equipment and therefore escorted them as far as Yan Hai.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they met a party delivering military equipment and escorted them as far as Yan Hai.

sentences.zh: 及入見，帝喜曰：「人言汝陷賊，乃能來耶！」

translations.literal: When he entered for audience the emperor rejoiced and said: "Men say you fell into the bandits' hands—yet you could come!"
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience the emperor said with delight, "Men said you had fallen into the enemy's hands—yet here you are!"

sentences.zh: 命與酒饌。

translations.literal: He ordered wine and food given.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered wine and food brought.

sentences.zh: 顧謂侍臣曰：「譬諸畜犬，得美食而棄其主，怯伯是也。

translations.literal: Turning to the attendants he said: "It is like a domestic dog that gets fine food and abandons its master—Qiebo is such a one.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendants he said, "It is like a house dog that takes good food and abandons its master. Qiebo is such a one.

sentences.zh: 雖未得食而不忘其主，此人是也。」

translations.literal: Though he has not yet gotten food he does not forget his master—this man is such a one."
translations.idiomatic: Though he has not yet been fed, he has not forgotten his master. This man is such a one."

sentences.zh: 更其名曰察罕斡脫赤，賜以鈔五千貫，頓首辭謝，乞以所賜與同來者。

translations.literal: His name was changed to Chahanwotuochi and five thousand strings of paper currency were granted; he bowed his head in thanks and begged to give what was granted to those who had come with him.
translations.idiomatic: His name was changed to Chahanwotuochi and he was granted five thousand strings of paper currency. He bowed in thanks and asked that the gift be shared with those who had come with him.

sentences.zh: 帝特命受之，而令中書定其同來者之賞有差。

translations.literal: The emperor specially ordered him to accept it himself and commanded the Secretariat to fix differentiated rewards for those who had come with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor insisted that he keep it himself and ordered the Secretariat to fix differentiated rewards for his companions.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，遷正奉大夫、河東山西道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Grand Master of Correct Service and pacification commissioner of the Hedong and Shanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he was transferred to Grand Master of Correct Service and pacification commissioner of the Hedong and Shanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「臣累戰而歸，衣裘盡弊。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your servant has returned from repeated battles and his fur garments are all worn out.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "I have returned from repeated campaigns and my fur garments are worn out.

sentences.zh: 河東，臣故鄉也，願乞錦衣以為榮。」

translations.literal: Hedong is your servant's native place; he wishes to beg brocade robes as honor."
translations.idiomatic: Hedong is my native place. I beg brocade robes as an honor to wear home."

sentences.zh: 帝以金織文衣賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted him gold-woven patterned robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him gold-woven patterned robes.

sentences.zh: 居二年，召還，帝諭之曰：「自此而北，乃顏故地曰阿八剌忽者，產魚，吾今立城，而以兀速、憨哈納思、乞里吉思三部人居之，名其城曰肇州。

translations.literal: After two years he was recalled; the emperor instructed him: "From here northward is Nayan's old territory called Abalahu, which produces fish; I now establish a city and settle the three tribes Usu, Hanhanasi, and Kirghiz there, naming the city Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled. The emperor told him, "North of here lies Nayan's old territory called Abalahu, which abounds in fish. I am founding a city there and settling the Usu, Hanhanasi, and Kirghiz tribes in it. The city will be called Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 汝往為宣慰使，仍別賜汝名曰小龍兒，或曰哈剌八都魯，汝可自擇之。」

translations.literal: You shall go as pacification commissioner, and I further grant you separately the name Little Dragon Son, or else Halabadoulu—you may choose for yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Go as pacification commissioner. I further grant you a new name—Little Dragon, or Halabadoulu. Choose as you will."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「龍，非臣下所敢承。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Dragon is not what a subject dares to bear."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Dragon is not a name a subject may dare to bear."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則哈剌八都魯可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Then Halabadoulu will do."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then Halabadoulu will do."

sentences.zh: 复賜以繡衣、玉帶，及鈔五千貫，其為人主所眷注如此。

translations.literal: He was again granted embroidered robes, a jade belt, and five thousand strings of paper currency—such was the sovereign's regard for him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again granted embroidered robes, a jade belt, and five thousand strings of paper currency. Such was the favor in which his sovereign held him.

sentences.zh: 既至，定市裡，安民居。

translations.literal: Once he arrived he fixed market wards and settled the people's dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he laid out the market wards and settled the people in their homes.

sentences.zh: 一日，得魚九尾，皆千斤，遣使來獻。

translations.literal: One day he obtained nine fish, each a thousand jin, and sent envoys to present them.
translations.idiomatic: One day he caught nine fish, each weighing a thousand jin, and sent them to court as tribute.

sentences.zh: 俄召還。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 三十一年春，世祖崩，太傅伯顏奉皇太后旨，命之曰：「東方汝嘗鎮之，今以屬汝，勿俟制命。」

translations.literal: In spring of the thirty-first year the Founder died; Grand Tutor Bayan, following the empress dowager's command, ordered him: "The east you once governed—now it is entrusted to you; do not await formal appointment."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-first year Kublai died. Grand Tutor Bayan, acting on the empress dowager's orders, told him, "You once governed the east. It is yours again now. Do not wait for formal appointment."

sentences.zh: 乃以為咸平宣慰使。

translations.literal: He was therefore made pacification commissioner of Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly appointed pacification commissioner of Xianping.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，召為御史中丞，行至懿州，病卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was summoned as censor-in-chief; traveling as far as Yizhou he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuanzhen era he was summoned to serve as censor-in-chief but died of illness at Yizhou on the journey.

sentences.zh: ○石抹明里

translations.literal: Shi Momingli
translations.idiomatic: Shi Momingli

sentences.zh: 石抹明里，契丹人，姓石抹，世典內膳。

translations.literal: Shi Momingli was a Khitan, surname Shi Mo, his family for generations overseeing the inner kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Momingli was a Khitan of the Shi Mo clan whose family had for generations overseen the imperial kitchen.

sentences.zh: 國製，內膳為近臣，非篤敬素著者不得為。

translations.literal: By state regulation the inner kitchen was for close attendants—only those of established deep respect could hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: By state regulation the inner kitchen was reserved for close attendants, and only men of proven devotion and long-standing reputation could hold the post.

sentences.zh: 明里祖曷魯，事太祖，睿宗嘗求之於帝，帝聽以其僚十人往，敕之曰：「皇子方總兵辟地，朕輟爾以事之。

translations.literal: Momingli's grandfather Helu served the Taizu; Prince Ruizong once requested him from the emperor, and the emperor permitted ten of his staff to go, charging them: "The prince is now commanding troops to open territory—I release you to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Momingli's grandfather Helu had served Taizu. When Prince Ruizong asked the emperor for him, the emperor allowed ten of his staff to go and charged them, "The prince is now commanding troops to open new territory. I release you to serve him.

sentences.zh: 能以事朕之恭事之，將用黃金覆周汝身矣。」

translations.literal: If you can serve him with the respect with which you serve me, I shall cover your whole body in gold."
translations.idiomatic: Serve him with the same respect you show me, and I shall cover your whole body in gold."

sentences.zh: 顯懿莊聖皇后語憲宗、世祖曰：「曷魯事太祖，聖躬或小不豫，其烹庖之精，百倍平日，汝兄弟當終始遇之。」

translations.literal: Empress Xianyi Zhuangsheng told Qa'an and the Founder: "Helu served the Taizu; when the sacred person had the slightest indisposition, the fineness of his cooking was a hundredfold the usual day—you brothers should treat him with constant favor to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xianyi Zhuangsheng told Qa'an and Kublai, "Helu served Taizu. Whenever the sovereign's health faltered even slightly, his cooking was a hundred times finer than on ordinary days. You brothers must treat him with constant favor to the end."

sentences.zh: 睿宗嘗從太宗西征，在道絕汲，曷魯晨起，聚草上霜，煮羹以進。

translations.literal: Prince Ruizong once followed Taizong on the western campaign; on the road water was utterly cut off; Helu rose early, gathered frost from the grass, boiled broth and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ruizong followed Taizong on the western campaign the army ran out of water on the march. Helu rose early, gathered frost from the grass, boiled it into broth, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 睿宗問曰：「何從得水？」

translations.literal: Prince Ruizong asked: "Whence did you get water?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked, "Where did you find water?"

sentences.zh: 因告之故，師還，賜金帛甚厚。

translations.literal: He then told the reason; when the army returned very generous gold and silks were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He explained how it was done. When the army returned he was rewarded with lavish gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 年八十卒。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 中統初，明里入見，世祖令侍臣送明里於裕宗，且曰：「明里，朕親臣之子也，今以事汝，令典膳事。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongtong Momingli entered for audience; the Founder ordered attendants to send Momingli to Prince Yuzong and said: "Momingli is the son of my close minister—I now assign him to serve you; let him oversee provision affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhongtong era Momingli was presented at court. Kublai had his attendants send him to Prince Yuzong and said, "Momingli is the son of my close minister. I assign him to you now to oversee provision affairs."

sentences.zh: 已而世祖嘗命裕宗：令從人十人來，朕將行賞焉。

translations.literal: Later the Founder once ordered Prince Yuzong: "Send ten followers—I shall bestow rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Later Kublai once ordered Prince Yuzong, "Send ten of your followers. I shall reward them."

sentences.zh: 十人者至帝前，四人列於明里上，帝曰：「第五人非明里耶？」

translations.literal: The ten came before the emperor; four were ranked above Momingli; the emperor said: "Is not the fifth Momingli?"
translations.idiomatic: When the ten came before the emperor, four were ranked above Momingli. The emperor said, "Is not the fifth Momingli?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「然。」

translations.literal: They replied: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "It is."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「上之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Move him up."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Move him up."

sentences.zh: 明里越一人立，帝又曰： 「更上之。」

translations.literal: Momingli stepped past one man and stood; the emperor again said: "Move him higher still."
translations.idiomatic: Momingli stepped past one man. The emperor said again, "Higher still."

sentences.zh: 明里又越一人立，帝曰：「止。」

translations.literal: Momingli again stepped past one man and stood; the emperor said: "Stop."
translations.idiomatic: Momingli stepped past another man. The emperor said, "Stop."

sentences.zh: 賜金紋衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was granted one suit of gold-patterned robes.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a suit of gold-patterned robes.

sentences.zh: 明里出，侍臣以明里後來反居上，相與耳語，帝聞之曰：「明里之祖曷魯，事太祖、睿宗以及朕兄弟，爾時汝輩安在？

translations.literal: When Momingli went out the attendants, because Momingli had come later yet stood above others, whispered among themselves; the emperor heard and said: "Momingli's grandfather Helu served the Taizu, Prince Ruizong, and us brothers—where were you lot then?
translations.idiomatic: When Momingli left, the attendants whispered among themselves that he had arrived last yet been placed above others. The emperor overheard and said, "Momingli's grandfather Helu served Taizu, Prince Ruizong, and us brothers. Where were you then?

sentences.zh: 顧謂後來耶！」

translations.literal: Yet you call him 'later'!"
translations.idiomatic: And you call him a latecomer!"

sentences.zh: 帝親討反者於北方，明里請備持矛，師還第功，賜白金百兩。

translations.literal: The emperor personally campaigned against rebels in the north; Momingli requested to stand ready with spear; when the army returned rewards were ranked by merit and he was granted a hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned in person against northern rebels, Momingli asked to stand ready with a spear. When the army returned he was rewarded according to merit with a hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 至元二十八年，為典膳令。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan he became Director of Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of the Zhiyuan era he was appointed director of provisions.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，加朝列大夫，賜金帶，又賜御衣一襲、鈔萬五千貫，詔曰：「明里舊臣，其令諸子入宿衛，可假禮部尚書，進階嘉議大夫，食尚書祿以老。」

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne he was given the additional rank of Grandee of the Court Assembly, granted a gold belt, and again granted one suit of imperial robes and fifteen thousand strings of paper currency; an edict said: "Momingli is an old minister—let his sons enter the palace guard; he may act as Minister of Rites, be advanced to Grand Master of Advising Counsel, and draw a minister's salary in retirement."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne he was given the additional rank of Grandee of the Court Assembly and granted a gold belt, an imperial robe, and fifteen thousand strings of paper currency. An edict read, "Momingli is an old minister. Let his sons enter the palace guard. He may act as Minister of Rites, be advanced to Grand Master of Advising Counsel, and draw a minister's salary in retirement."

sentences.zh: 武​​宗即位，詔曰：「明里夫婦，歷事帝后，保抱朕躬，朕甚德之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne an edict said: "Momingli and his wife have served emperors and empresses through the ages and nursed my person—I am deeply obliged to them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne an edict read, "Momingli and his wife have served emperors and empresses through the ages and nursed my person. I am deeply obliged to them.

sentences.zh: 可特令明里榮祿大夫、司徒；

translations.literal: Momingli may specially be made Grand Master of Glorious Emolument and Grand Minister of Education;
translations.idiomatic: Momingli is specially appointed Grand Master of Glorious Emolument and Grand Minister of Education;

sentences.zh: 其妻梅仙封順國夫人。

translations.literal: his wife Meixian is enfeoffed as Lady of Shunguo.
translations.idiomatic: and his wife Meixian is enfeoffed as Lady of Shunguo.

sentences.zh: 賜黃金二百五十兩、白金千五百兩、衣一襲。」

translations.literal: Two hundred fifty taels of gold, fifteen hundred taels of silver, and one suit of robes are granted."
translations.idiomatic: They are granted two hundred fifty taels of gold, fifteen hundred taels of silver, and one suit of robes."

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，語宮人曰：「昔朕有疾甚危，徽仁裕聖皇后憂之，梅仙守視，不解帶者七十日。

translations.literal: Renzong, while in the Eastern Palace, told palace women: "Once when I was gravely ill Empress Huiren Yusheng was deeply concerned; Meixian attended and for seventy days did not unfasten her belt.
translations.idiomatic: While still in the Eastern Palace, Renzong told the palace women, "Once when I was gravely ill Empress Huiren Yusheng was deeply worried. Meixian attended me and for seventy days never unfastened her belt.

sentences.zh: 今不敢忘，其賜明里寶帶、錦衣、輿及四騾。」

translations.literal: Now I dare not forget—grant Momingli a jeweled belt, brocade robes, a carriage, and four mules."
translations.idiomatic: I dare not forget that now. Grant Momingli a jeweled belt, brocade robes, a carriage, and four mules."

sentences.zh: 至大三年二月卒，年六十有九。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Zhida he died, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the third year of the Zhida era at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子皆顯貴。

translations.literal: His sons all reached eminent rank.
translations.idiomatic: His sons all rose to eminent rank.

sentences.zh: ○謝仲溫

translations.literal: Xie Zhongwen
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhongwen

sentences.zh: 謝仲溫，字君玉，豐州豐縣人。

translations.literal: Xie Zhongwen, styled Junyu, was a native of Feng County in Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhongwen, whose style name was Junyu, was a native of Feng County in Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父睦歡，以貲雄鄉曲間，大兵南下，轉客兀剌城。

translations.literal: His father Muhuan, by wealth dominant among the villages of the district, when the great army came south moved as a guest to Wula City.
translations.idiomatic: His father Muhuan, a man whose wealth made him dominant in the local countryside, moved his household to Wula City when the great army marched south.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻西夏，過其城，睦歡與其帥迎降。

translations.literal: When the Taizu attacked Western Xia and passed his city, Muhuan and its commander came out to welcome and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu attacked Western Xia and passed his city, Muhuan and its commander came out to welcome the army and surrender.

sentences.zh: 從攻西京，睦歡力戰先登，連中三矢，僕城下。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Western Capital, Muhuan fought fiercely and was first to scale the wall, was struck by three arrows in succession, and fell beneath the wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the assault on Western Capital he fought fiercely and was first to scale the wall. Three arrows struck him in succession and he fell beneath the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 太宗見而憐之，命軍校拔其矢，縛牛，刳其腸，裸而納諸牛腹中，良久乃蘇，誓以死報，每遇敵，必身先之，官至太原路金銀鐵冶達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Taizong saw this and pitied him, ordered a military officer to pull out the arrows, bound an ox, cut open its belly, stripped him naked and placed him in the ox's belly; after a long while he revived, swore to repay with his death, and whenever he met the enemy always went before the rest; he reached office as darughachi of gold, silver, and iron smelting on the Taiyuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong saw him and took pity. He ordered the arrows drawn, an ox bound and its belly opened, and Muhuan placed naked inside the carcass. After a long while he revived, swore to repay the favor with his life, and ever after led the charge against every enemy. He rose to darughachi of gold, silver, and iron smelting on the Taiyuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，入見，帝曰：「汝非謝仲溫乎？

translations.literal: In spring of the thirtieth year he entered for audience; the emperor said: "Are you not Xie Zhongwen?
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirtieth year he was received in audience. The emperor said, "Are you not Xie Zhongwen?

sentences.zh: 朕謂汝死矣！」

translations.literal: I thought you were dead!"
translations.idiomatic: I thought you were dead!"

sentences.zh: 從容語及攻鄂時事，帝喜甚，諭曰：「汝將復官乎？

translations.literal: At ease he spoke of affairs when E was attacked; the emperor was greatly pleased and instructed: "Will you take office again?
translations.idiomatic: He spoke at ease of the campaign against Ezhou, to the emperor's great delight. The emperor said, "Will you take office again?

sentences.zh: 朕當為卿擇之。」

translations.literal: I shall choose one for you."
translations.idiomatic: I shall choose a post for you."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣老矣，無能為也，一子早亡，惟有孫孛完，幸陛下憐之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant is old and can do nothing; one son died early, and there is only the grandson Bowan—may Your Majesty pity him."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I am old and good for nothing now. One son died young, and I have only my grandson Bowan. I beg Your Majesty to show him favor."

sentences.zh: 即日命備宿衛。

translations.literal: That same day he was ordered to stand ready in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Bowan was ordered into the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 大德六年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dade he died, age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of the Dade era at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 子蘭，江浙達魯花赤，先卒。

translations.literal: His son Lan was darughachi of Jiangzhe and died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan, darughachi of Jiangzhe, had died earlier.

sentences.zh: 孫孛完，承事郎、冀寧等路管民提舉司達魯花赤。

translations.literal: His grandson Bowan was Gentleman for Attending Affairs and darughachi of the Bureau for Overseeing the People of Jining and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Bowan served as Gentleman for Attending Affairs and darughachi of the bureau for overseeing the people on the Jining and other circuits.

sentences.zh: ○高觿

translations.literal: Gao Xi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xi

sentences.zh: 高觿，字彥解，渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Xi, styled Yanjie, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xi, whose style name was Yanjie, was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 世仕金，祖彝，徙居上黨。

translations.literal: His family served Jin for generations; his grandfather Yi moved to reside in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served the Jin for generations. His grandfather Yi relocated to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 父守忠，國初為千戶。

translations.literal: His father Shouzhong was a chiliarch at the beginning of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shouzhong was a chiliarch in the early years of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 太宗九年，從親王口溫不花攻黃州，歿於兵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taizong he followed Prince Köten in attacking Huangzhou and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taizong's reign he followed Prince Köten in the attack on Huangzhou and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 觿事世祖，備宿衛，頗見親幸。

translations.literal: Xi served the Founder, stood ready in the palace guard, and was rather favored.
translations.idiomatic: Xi served Kublai in the palace guard and enjoyed considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 至元初，立燕王為皇太子，詔選才雋士充官屬，以觿掌藝文，兼領中醖、宮衛監門事，又監作皇太子宮，規制有法，帝嘉之，錫以金幣、厩馬，因賜名失剌。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhiyuan the Prince of Yan was established as crown prince; an edict selected talented scholars to fill his staff; Xi was put in charge of literary arts, concurrently headed central brewing and palace gate guard affairs, and also supervised construction of the crown prince's palace with regulated standards; the emperor praised this and granted gold and currency and stable horses, thereby granting the name Shila.
